title: Search order: organise by mechanism, not by position (P1 to P18, November 9 to 17, 2026)
scope: Seventeen small preregistered steps on the older Gen2 swarm's search order (P1 to P17), reads of recorded Gen3 outcomes, and one follow-up replay in Gen3's next-test step (P18). Aggregate counts and ratios only. The swarm's original sweep method, the recorded mission data and the mission's name stay private; mechanisms are anonymised.
generation: Gen2 work (the legacy swarm); its lesson is carried forward to Gen3

evidence_labels.scripted: measured on fixtures, no quantum-computer time: scripted test targets with a known answer, scored by code; no model, no real target
evidence_labels.measured_on_ibm_hardware: one run on a real IBM device (P7), billed seconds from IBM's usage record
evidence_labels.measured_recorded: a read of recorded Gen3 outcomes (P14 not blind; the P15 replay blind; P18 an off-policy replay of recorded verdicts)

lesson: Organise search by mechanism (the kind of attack), not by where a candidate sits in a list.
evidence_for_the_lesson: recorded Gen3 outcomes point this way: the mechanism predicts 111 of 125 recorded checks (not blind)
the Nano lockpick's scripted-reader result (L0) agrees: it searches by the features of a stuck state
the scripted steps (P13 to P17) assume outcomes follow the mechanism and measure what searching by it is worth

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: does the swarm's original sweep order home in on the good areas of a test field?
steps.result: no: its final focus zone held fewer good items than random at every size; narrowing's zone also fell short (it met the line at 1 of 3 sizes; the gate needed 2)

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: narrowing against random order where good items sit together
steps.result: narrowing found 15.9, 15.4 and 14.9 times as many good items as random order at three sizes; the original order 3.6 to 4.8 times

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: the same on messier fields (off-grid, jittered)
steps.result: 13.5 to 14.5 times random on the messiest fields; 18.7 to 20.6 on aligned ones

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: fields built from banked Gen3 task evidence (80 tasks)
steps.result: 7.5, 4.5 and 9.6 times random at drive lengths 6, 7 and 8 (above 1.5 at all three lengths; length 7 failed only the significance check)

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: 200 fresh tasks, with read noise and dropouts
steps.result: 10.2 and 9.4 times random clean; 8.5 to 10.1 with noise; 7.9 to 8.7 with dropouts

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: narrowing as a hint inside a scripted solver: fewer solver steps?
steps.result: no: 1.10 and 1.06 against the solver's own search, and the hint cost more to make than it saved

steps.label: measured_on_ibm_hardware
steps.question: narrowing on IBM hardware: good candidates per billed second against random order
steps.result: 1.7 and 3.4 times as many good candidates per billed second as random order, at two sizes; 27.0 billed seconds over six jobs; 85 percent of probe indices delivered exactly (one unstable qubit); the hardware only carried the probe indices, with no quantum computation in the search, and at drive length 7 the line was passed by one billed second per job

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: a hardware repeat with a bad-qubit screen
steps.result: the offline gate passed; the live repeat was never released or run
steps.verdict: offline gate MET; live cells NOT RUN

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: does aligning the sweep make it a solver?
steps.result: no: an aligned sweep solved 4.8 and 4.0 times as many tasks as the unaligned order, but only 0.48 and 0.24 of them against a 0.50 line

steps.label: built
steps.question: wire narrowing into the swarm behind a setting
steps.result: built; off by default at the time

steps.label: built
steps.question: a Gen3 probe-mission driver that can use narrowing
steps.result: built and tested; nothing calls it yet

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: inside the real swarm loop: narrowing against the original order
steps.result: 6.6 times as many good items (2.2 times from the order alone, the rest from sweeping the list's real length); the original order only ever moved on when its time ran out (200 of 200 sessions) and in 9 of 200 sessions sent 3 of 5 agents past the end of the list

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: on the swarm's real list order, with outcomes driven by technique
steps.result: no difference from the original order (0.95) and below no sweep at all (0.77): the list spreads each technique's variants evenly through its category, so position carries little; narrowing became the default under the preregistered rule

steps.label: measured_recorded
steps.question: what decides success in recorded Gen3 outcomes?
steps.result: the mechanism: it predicts 111 of 125 recorded checks (permutation p 0.00001); the best 3 of 17 mechanisms hold 65 percent of the hits on 34 percent of the checks; a technique-grouped list won big on some targets and lost on most, so it was not shipped
steps.verdict: Part R MET (not blind); the grouped list only above, not shipped

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: try every technique once, then focus
steps.result: 200 of 200 test targets reached against 68 percent with no sweep, and 5.4 times the hits; narrowing by position reached fewer targets than no sweep (0.535 to 0.620 against 0.710); run at the old 15 percent explore rate
steps.verdict: MET; shipped as the swarm default

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: how much to explore against how much to dig
steps.result: exploring 90 percent of the time found the most mechanisms per target: 0.660 against 0.600 for pure exploring and 0.392 for pure digging; the old setting explored 15 percent; total hits fall as exploring rises (1,723 at 90/10 against 2,896 all digging), so the mix trades repeat finds for coverage

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: does 90/10 hold when the share of working variants changes?
steps.result: yes: its worst loss against the best rate was 0.012 across shares from 5 to 100 percent

steps.label: measured_recorded
steps.question: the mechanism-first rule against Gen3's current next-test rule, replayed on recorded missions
steps.result: on the one mission large enough to count, it reached all 12 mechanisms that hit in the record, against 11 for the current rule; the win rests on one mechanism that missed first and hit later, which the current rule drops after one miss; two smaller missions were not counted (one more win, one tie)
steps.verdict: SHIP by the preregistered rule; not wired into Gen3 yet

recorded_outcomes.label: measured_recorded
recorded_outcomes.source: one Gen3 private security mission; local reproductions; no live target; mechanisms anonymised as M01 to M17
recorded_outcomes.caveat: the counts were seen before the preregistration, and promising mechanisms were tested more often

blind_replay_p15.what: the same recorded verdicts read in two orders (reported, not gated)
blind_replay_p15.reading: trying every mechanism in turn reaches almost twice as many mechanisms early; the mission's own order finds more hits early because it kept digging where it had already found something

replay_p18.label: measured_recorded
replay_p18.what: an off-policy replay: each rule may take only tests the mission recorded; budget three tests per mechanism
replay_p18.why: one late finder: a mechanism whose first recorded test missed and which hit later; the current rule drops a candidate after one miss
replay_p18.hits_not_comparable: the current rule ran out of recorded tests after 23 of 51, so only the mechanism count is a fair comparison
replay_p18.uncounted: two smaller missions: one more win, one tie
current_rule_properties_exposed: every hit scores the same, so ties are broken by candidate id
it scores only a candidate's latest test, with no memory of its record
replay_p18.not_wired: Gen3's next-test step works in cycles with a shrinking fanout, while the tested rule is test by test; the cycle form must be built and replayed first

explore_ratio_p16_p17.label: scripted
explore_ratio_p16_p17.caveat: the test targets use invented numbers (open techniques per target, share of working variants); P17 varied the working share

hardware_p7.label: measured_on_ibm_hardware
hardware_p7.route: direct IBM runtime from a laptop, not Predator's production route
hardware_p7.limits: one run, one device, one calibration window, no repeat; scripted fields; no solver gain; no quantum advantage

shipped.where: draft pull request #489 in the private repository, into a feature branch, not main
defaults: the swarm's list is grouped by technique
the swarm tries every technique once, then focuses (P15, run at the old 15 percent explore rate)
the swarm explores 90 percent of the time (P16; was 15 percent)
shipped.switch_back: settings switch each change back; the list order and the sweep must be switched back together

kept_private_for_the_loop: a held-out set of 17 recorded mechanisms, to score a future Model 1 choice of which mechanism to test next
879 narrowing steps logged on the scripted test fields (P14), which could become replayable steps in Atlas
what_it_does_not_do: it is Gen2 work on the legacy swarm
the test targets were scripted: no real judge and no real target
nothing was replayed or trained into Model 1
it does not touch the Gen4 test (each Model 1 generation reaching further with fewer outside rescues)
still_open: a smaller swarm defect wastes 2.7 percent of turns at the old 15 percent explore rate (about 0.3 percent at the shipped 90 percent) when a focus zone is smaller than the number of agents
the live hardware repeat (P8) was never run
the Gen3 probe-mission driver (P11) has no caller
the P18 rule has no caller: Gen3's next-test step works in cycles, so a cycle form must be built and replayed first
claims_boundary: Scripted test targets except P7 (one IBM hardware run) and the reads and replay of recorded Gen3 outcomes. No real target was contacted. No quantum advantage. Nothing here is a Model 1 result.
next: P18 ran the proposed step as a replay and passed its preregistered ship rule on one mission. Next: build the rule's cycle form as an opt-in Gen3 rule, replay it on the same frozen missions, and only then offer it.
